review: Numerical Differential Equations and Stochastic Dynamics rendering audit
screenshot_review: Every assigned title and complete ItemBody was reviewed against the frozen source/snapshot and its individual original-resolution screenshot tile(s). All 104 receipt-listed PNGs were opened individually with tools.view_image(detail="original"); no collage or downscaled view was used. Long items continue across sequential screenshot captures; apparent tile boundaries were checked against the continuation and are not clipping.

diagram_candidates.kind: potentially useful directed graph/SCC decomposition diagram
diagram_candidates.why: The algorithm defines a positive-transition graph, computes strongly connected components, and distinguishes closed communicating classes from transient components. A small illustrative graph with SCC boundaries could clarify the direction convention and closure test, but the prose and matrix formulas are complete; this is an editorial candidate, not a defect.
diagram_candidates.content_to_draw: Use a finite example column-stochastic P and draw j→i exactly when P_ij>0. Show one closed SCC C with no outgoing edges to S\C and a transient SCC with a path to C. Label row-transition K=P^T and ensure K_ij=P_ji so the same graph is i→j under row-source convention. Use distinct edge arrows and mark any self-loops consistently; demonstrate SCC condensation without implying a general stochastic-chain diagram.

diagram_candidates.kind: potentially useful multiple-shooting mesh and residual diagram
diagram_candidates.why: The algorithm has approximate segment maps, continuity residuals, endpoint boundary residual, and a finite-budget Newton update. A labeled mesh picture could distinguish segment starts and computed endpoint matches; the source already gives the exact row convention.
diagram_candidates.content_to_draw: Draw a<t_0<…<t_N=b with segment-start unknowns s_0,…,s_N, arrows labeled tilde-Phi_i from s_i to its computed endpoint, residual arrows/labels tilde-Phi_i(s_i)-s_{i+1} for i=0,…,N−1, and terminal boundary block B(s_0,s_N). Indicate the residual vector is square in (N+1)d variables. Do not imply approximate segment trajectories necessarily join or certify an exact BVP solution; line 37 explicitly disclaims that.

existing_diagram_checks.check: The graph orientation is consistent: source-state j to target-state i iff P_ij>0. With K=P^T, K_ij=P_ji is the row transition probability from i to j; the closure test K_ij=0 for i in C, j outside C forbids edges leaving C. The two-way reachability condition R_ij and R_ji correctly identifies SCC membership. Checked source lines 27–33 and the individual tile; no existing diagram is present.

The segment residual direction is flow endpoint Phi_{s_{i+1}-s_i}(u_i) minus next node u_{i+1}, with 0≤i<N; the terminal block B(u_0,u_N) uses x_N−x_0 and phase psi(x_0). The augmented field (theta f(x),0) preserves theta along each segment. The normalized midpoint residual is (u_{i+1}−u_i)/h−f_tilde((u_i+u_{i+1})/2), also with 0≤i<N. Signs, domains, indices, and square dimension match source lines 37–49. No existing diagram is present.

The displayed barrier event is inf B≤c (downward crossing); the formula exp(−2(x−c)(y−c)/h) uses nonnegative endpoint distances and gives 1 when either endpoint lies on the barrier. The reflection proof maps the downward crossing to a centered bridge maximum event with positive level x−c. Checked source lines 30–36, 52–60 and individual tiles; no existing diagram is present.

diagram_review: No TikZ diagrams or diagram failures were recorded in the 66 assigned screenshot receipts. Inline graph/map relations were checked as enumerated above. The two diagram candidates are optional and source-supported; they do not indicate missing mathematical content.
clipping: No confirmed clipping. Every assigned receipt tile was opened separately at original resolution. Tall bodies split across sequential captures; the overlapping continuation shows no lost content.
reference_titles: Wikilink references appear as separate block lines in the captured card presentation. No unexpected reference-title leakage or item-ID issue was observed.
technique_banners: CSS technique banners are presentation chrome; no rendering issue was observed.
limitations: Local frozen sources, snapshots, static HTML, screenshot receipts and PNGs only; no live site, browser, or network inspection.
This is a rendering and focused diagram-relation review, not a full mathematical proof audit of every assigned item.
